Subject: Acme - access proof pack & export format (follow-up)

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the audit evidence you requested around who-accessed-what/when.

Recap of ask (from your security questionnaire):
- A sample export showing user/service identity, resource (model/route), timestamp, action (read/generate/retrieve), request id, and anonymized token counts
- CSV or Parquet preferred, with timezone in ISO8601 UTC and a column indicating whether the data included any PII markers
- Retention policy options (30/90/365 days) and the mechanism for on-demand exports for eDiscovery

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben and Marissa: can you confirm we can produce a 24-hour sample slice in the requested CSV schema and attach a short schema doc?
2) Lena: if CSV looks good we’ll deliver a sample export and an explanation of how we hash/ salt identifiers for tenant-level audit reviewing
3) If acceptable, we’ll add an automated scheduled dump and a playbook describing how to produce longer range exports for legal/forensics

I’ll aim to get a preliminary sample to you by EOD Thu (11/05). If you need it sooner, tell me and we’ll prioritize.

Best,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Lena Gomez <lena.gomez@acme-payments.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - access proof pack & export format (follow-up)

Thanks Maya — that summary is perfect. A couple of clarifications from our InfoSec side: 

1) PII flagging: we need a boolean column (pii_flag) and a secondary column (pii_type) with categories (email, name, payment_token, other). If pii_flag is true we do NOT need the raw PII value (redact or replace with consistent pseudonym).

2) Time range: please include a timezone-normalized timestamp (UTC) and the original event_time zone if you capture it.

3) Provenance: include a column for the model_version/id and whether the request was routed through a cache (cache_hit true/false).

4) Chain-of-access: if a human viewed generated content in the console (not just API requests), include a viewer_id and action_type (view/download).

Regarding retention: we expect a default 90-day retention but need confirmation that exports can be generated for arbitrary historical windows within contractual retention. Also: do you offer an export hash verification (SHA256) for integrity?

If you can send the CSV sample plus the schema doc, we’ll route to our compliance team. Thanks — Lena

On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 09:21 AM -0800, Lena Gomez <lena.gomez@acme-payments.com> wrote:

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - access proof pack & export format (follow-up)

Maya / Marissa — tagging in. We can produce the requested columns. Quick notes on implementation: 

- Schema: see attached PDF (redwood_audit_schema_v1.pdf). It includes columns: event_id, tenant_id_hash, user_id_hash, viewer_id_hash, model_id, route, event_timestamp_utc, original_timezone, action_type, cache_hit, pii_flag, pii_type, pii_pseudonym, request_id, token_count_estimate
- Pseudonyms: we produce stable pseudonyms per-tenant using HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific salt (so the same user maps consistently across exports but remains non-reversible to Acme). We can additionally redact entirely if they prefer.
- Exports: we can deliver CSV or Parquet. CSV will be faster for initial review; Parquet recommended for large windows due to compression and schema typing.
- Integrity: we can provide a SHA256 checksum per-file and sign it with a Redwood internal key. We can also produce a manifest JSON with file-level checksums.
- Retention: default hosted retention is 90 days for audit logs; we can configure 30/90/365 for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted accounts we can add contractual language for extended retention at commit.

Maya — I’ll assemble a 24-hour sample (CSV) with the pseudonymized identifiers and attach it. Marissa, can you double-check the console view events (viewer_id) are included in the sample for one day?

-Ben

--
